claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase material.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi alloy is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi at 500–600 °C causes diffusion-driven elemental segregation.
Aging-induced segregation leads to secondary-phase precipitation at grain boundaries.
Intermediate-temperature atomic mobility permits segregation and nucleation of brittle phases at grain boundaries or within the matrix.
The secondary precipitates embrittle grain boundaries or interphase interfaces.
The precipitates act as stress concentrators under mechanical loading.
Precipitate-induced stress concentration promotes intergranular cracking.
Aging-induced phase evolution decreases ductility and fracture toughness.
Aging-induced phase evolution can cause brittle fracture under mechanical loading.
The untreated as-cast baseline exhibits ductile deformation and high or superior toughness under standard conditions.
Relative to identically loaded as-cast controls, aged specimens will have lower fracture toughness.
Relative to identically loaded as-cast controls, aged specimens will initiate cracks earlier.
Aged specimens will tend toward brittle intergranular fracture.
The proposed embrittlement will be most significant during long-term intermediate-temperature exposure combined with cyclic or sustained mechanical loading.
Slight compositional adjustments can alter aging thresholds, required aging durations, and precipitate volume fraction or morphology.
The mechanical response is sensitive to precipitate characteristics.

contradictions.description: The alloy is described simultaneously as a single-phase homogeneous solid solution and as a eutectic high-entropy alloy. Without clarification that 'eutectic' refers only to nominal composition rather than a eutectic multiphase microstructure, these descriptions are internally in tension.
